title: Seah Besteel Starts Mass Production of Robot Reducer Steel Previously Sourced Abroad
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · October 6, 2026

Seah Besteel has entered mass production of a specialty steel for robot reducer "flex splines," a core material that until now relied largely on foreign suppliers, especially Japanese ones. Here is what has been disclosed about the material and where it has already shipped.

CompanyRoleEvidence
Seah Besteel
KRX: 306200		Developed and now mass-produces flex spline steel for robot reducersReported: company announcement, Oct 6, 2026
SPG
KRX: 058610		Domestic precision reducer maker; first customer, supplied in Feb 2026 for industrial robotsReported: company announcement, Oct 6, 2026

What's been disclosed

  • The product: A specialty steel for the flex spline, a core part of a robot reducer. A reducer lowers motor rotation speed so a robot's limbs and legs can move precisely at the speed and force needed; a smaller gear clearance allows more precise motion.
  • Localization angle: The company says this material was previously dependent on a few foreign suppliers, particularly Japanese companies.
  • How it is made: Seah Besteel says it designed the alloy itself to reduce microscopic shape deformation during heat treatment while keeping machinability and dimensional precision, and uses vacuum refining with recirculation equipment to minimize non-metallic inclusions that cause micro-fractures. It says this improves cleanliness and fatigue life for repeated robot motion.
  • First supply: In February 2026 the material was first supplied to SPG, a domestic precision reducer company, for industrial robots.
  • Stage: The company announced on October 6, 2026 that it has entered mass production.
  • Next: Seah Besteel plans to develop additional specialty steel grades for humanoid robots and widen its product lineup.

What's still unconfirmed

The announcement gave no production volume, price, customer list beyond SPG, or the share of flex spline steel this would replace, and the performance claims come from the company itself. It also did not name the foreign suppliers. (Reported)

Quick FAQ

What is a flex spline?
It is a thin, flexible gear component inside a robot reducer. The reducer slows the motor's rotation so the robot can move its joints precisely.

Is the material already in robots?
It was first supplied to SPG for industrial robots in February 2026. Whether it is used in humanoid robots was not stated; the company says humanoid-specific grades are still to be developed.

Which company is this, Seah Besteel or Seah Besteel Holdings?
The report is about Seah Besteel (KRX: 306200), the steelmaker. Seah Besteel Holdings (KRX: 001430) is the separately listed holding company.
